summary: Iteration 42 backend testing — branded cover slide for PPT/PDF exports. Wrote 8 pytest tests covering: (1) PPTX project export first slide is branded cover with full-bleed navy rectangle, 'PROJECT STATUS REPORT' eyebrow, project name, 'For {client}', period+date, 'Prepared by DD Consulting', 'CONFIDENTIAL'. (2) WBS PPTX cover has 'WORK BREAKDOWN STRUCTURE' subtitle. (3) PDF export has cover+content pages (>=2) still at 16:9 (960x540pt). (4) Print URL JS bundle contains data-export-section='cover'. (5) _fetch_cover_meta returns fallback dict on invalid project_id (no crash). (6) Section slides no longer say 'Slide N'. All 8/8 tests passed.
critical_code_review_comments: ppt_export.py _fetch_cover_meta directly imports from `database` inside the function — OK for lazy import to avoid circular deps, but consider top-level typed dependency injection for testability.
The cover-slide layout uses absolute Inches positioning; if slide dimensions change (e.g., 4:3 fallback) elements would misalign. Currently fine since exports are hard-coded 16:9.
_fetch_cover_meta swallows ObjectId parsing exceptions silently — good for resilience, verified via test with 'nonexistent_id_xyz' returning fallback dict.
